question: How large is the Agave angustifolia chloroplast genome, and how many annotated genes does it hold?
expect: 157,274 bp; 132 genes (86 protein-coding, 38 tRNAs, 8 rRNAs) (Fig. 6 caption, p9)
rendered: According to the document, the Agave angustifolia chloroplast genome is approximately 157,274 base pairs (bp) in size. It exhibits a classic quadripartite structure of angiosperms, with a Large Single-Copy (LSC) region of 85,895 bp, a Small Single-Copy (SSC) region of 18,229 bp, and a pair of Inverted Repeats (IRs) spanning 26,575 bp each. Within this cp architecture, 132 annotated genes are highlighted, consisting of 86 protein-coding genes, 38 tRNAs, and 8 rRNAs.
